observation_summary: The NumericEntityUnescaper fails to correctly handle supplementary characters (Unicode code points > 0xFFFF) when unescaping numeric entities, resulting in incorrect character output.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the internal logic of the unescaping procedure to correctly handle supplementary characters by converting the entity value into a surrogate pair (two chars) when the value exceeds 0xFFFF. This is a procedural correction to the unescaping algorithm, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows an added conditional block that checks if the entityValue > 0xFFFF and then performs a specific conversion using Character.toChars() to write two characters instead of one.
The bug report describes that the current implementation treats each char as one character, which is incorrect for supplementary characters.
The failing test case confirms that the unescaper produces incorrect output for supplementary characters.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds an 'if' condition, the primary purpose is to implement the correct logic for handling supplementary characters, not to validate input or prevent an error.
The fix is a local procedural change within an existing method, not a design-level capability addition.
